title: Local-loop SDKenV Fail-Fast Manifesto and Quick Flows
body:
Purpose:

This document captures a compact, practitioner-friendly manifesto for the local SDKenV experience we want to ship: a predictable, fast feedback loop developers can run on their laptop that mirrors production behaviours (auth, routing, streaming, error modes) without requiring cloud/GPU dependencies.

Why this matters (problem statement):
- Engineers waste time waiting for remote deploys to validate simple changes (prompt tweaks, retry logic, telemetry hooks).
- Onboarding new SDK contributors is friction-heavy: env setup, token gating, and intermittent network failures slow discovery and experimentation.
- Many regressions that should be caught early slip into CI because local runs don’t exercise critical runtime behaviours (e.g., streaming chunks, KV cache warmups, prefix caching).

Goals (what "good" looks like):
1) 3-minute first loop from repo clone to a streamed response in local mode.
2) Local environment can simulate at least 80% of production failure/latency modes relevant to developer flows.
3) Minimal secrets exposure: ephemeral dev tokens and scoped proxies that can be revoked.
4) Telemetry parity: same trace ids and structured logs (locally sanitized) so developers see the same traces they will in prod.
5) Easy toggle between "dev-sim" (fast mocked responses) and "dev-live" (real-hosted API) with one config switch.

Principles (manifesto lines):
- Fail fast, observe faster: local runs should be noisy and explicit about errors. Surface stack traces, network timings and model quality deltas.
- Tiny reproducible loops: the minimal change -> run -> observe cycle should be under 3 minutes for most edits.
- Safety-by-default: local tooling favors short-lived tokens, sandboxed proxies, and sample datasets — no accidental spills to production.
- Deterministic dev fixtures: provide canned prompt datasets and expected output assertions to validate regressions before CI.

Persona and typical flows:
- New SDK contributor (Dev): clone, run bootstrap, call example app, iterate.
- Product engineer (PE): verify prompt change quality with sample user transcripts and compare embeddings/regressions locally.
- Integrator/Solutions engineer (SE): simulate burst traffic and test fallback routes with local-only tools.

Minimum reproducible experience (3-minute path):
Prereqs: git, docker (optional), node 18+/python 3.11, small CLI tool we ship (sdkenv).
Steps:
1) git clone git@github.com:redwood-inference/sdk.git && cd sdk/examples/simple-chat
2) sdkenv bootstrap --profile minimal  # sets ephemeral token, local proxy, fixtures
3) npm install && npm run dev-local  # example server starts on localhost:3000
4) open http://localhost:3000 and paste sample prompt or run curl to validate streaming chunk boundaries
Expected outcome: a streaming chat appears in the browser/terminal within ~20–30s, with telemetry link printed to console.

Commands (quick reference):
- sdkenv bootstrap --profile minimal  # configure ephemeral local tokens + fixtures
- sdkenv mode set [dev-sim|dev-live]  # toggle between mocked vs live API backends
- sdkenv trace tail --id <trace-id>  # follow local telemetry, mirrors Console trace view
- sdkenv inject-latency --p90 250  # simulate p90 latency in ms for downstream calls
- sdkenv reset  # clear local caches, kv stores, mock state

Local environment features (what sdkenv will provide):
- Scoped proxy that lands on localhost:5400 and rewrites host headers; dev token minted for 1 hour.
- Streaming shim: local server emits SSE/websocket chunks to replicate production chunking behaviour.
- KV cache emulator: small on-disk or in-memory store to reproduce cache warmup and eviction scenarios.
- Mock model harness: ability to swap in deterministic responses (seeded) or to forward to hosted model.
- Telemetry bridge: sends sanitized spans to local collector and optionally forwards trimmed events to Console for integrated traces.

Quality checks to include in local flows (pre-CI gating suggestions):
- smoke/streaming: confirm that the local client receives at least one chunk within 1s of first token generation.
- kv-warmup: after a seed run, the second run should show cache-hit telemetry for prefix lengths < 128 tokens.
- fallback-policy: force primary model to error and assert fallback model returns within configured timeout.
- regression-check: execute a curated prompt set and check top-n token log-prob deltas against baseline checkpoints (allow configurable tolerance).

Developer ergonomics & microcopy suggestions (UI/CLI):
- Console output should show: [sdkenv] profile=minimal token=ephemeral expires=2024-11-12T16:00Z
- Error message examples: "Model A timed out (500ms). Falling back to Model B — see trace: <url>"
- Quick hints printed once per session: "Try: sdkenv inject-latency --p90 500 to reproduce regional slowness"

Telemetry and observability (local parity):
- Trace ID propagation: local SDK runs must attach a trace id that can be pasted into Redwood Console to view timeline-like traces (with sanitized data).
- Event sampling: by default capture detailed spans for the first 5 local runs and then switch to summary sampling to avoid noise.
- Local log format: JSON-lines with these fields: ts, level, component, trace_id, local_span, msg. Keep schema consistent with production to make local/remote debugging easier.

Security & token model:
- Ephemeral tokens created by sdkenv are scoped to: project:examples/simple-chat, scope:read-write-demo, expiry:1h. Tokens are stored under ~/.sdkenv/tokens.json (file mode 600).
- For CI or external demo sharing, sdkenv can mint "shareable session" links that bootstrap a temporary proxy with an expiry and predetermined fixture set.

Troubleshooting (common issues and quick fixes):
- No streaming chunks: ensure proxy is running (sdkenv proxy status). If running behind corp VPN, add 127.0.0.1 to NO_PROXY.
- Permission errors on token file: chmod 600 ~/.sdkenv/tokens.json and re-run sdkenv bootstrap.
- Divergent model outputs vs hosted: toggle sdkenv mode set dev-live to confirm whether discrepancy is in local mock or hosting.
- Local cache not clearing: sdkenv reset --force clears on-disk cache.

Metrics & success signals (how we’ll measure adoption/impact):
- Time-to-first-stream (median) for new contributors < 3 minutes (instrument via onboarding telemetry).
- % of PRs with at least one local run of the curated prompt set before CI: target 65% in quarter-one.
- Number of support tickets caused by "environment mismatch" reduced by 40% after sdkenv adoption.
- Feedback loop score from new hires during onboarding sessions (survey question: "Were you able to get a working example in <10 minutes?") target 85% yes.

Integration checklist for example repos (simple-chat, embedder-demo, rerank-lab):
- add sdkenv profile file: .sdkenv/profile.json with hooks for bootstrap
- include fixtures/ (3–5 curated prompts + expected assertions)
- small README section "local loop" with exact commands and measurable expectations

Open questions & tradeoffs:
- How much fidelity do we want for model sampling locally vs keeping run-time fast? (Mocked deterministic responses speed up loops but hide model-quality regressions.)
- Do we include a small on-disk quantized model for more realistic latency? Pros: catches perf regressions; Cons: increases repo size and local resource requirements.
- Governance for shareable sessions — who can mint and for how long?

Next steps (actionable):
1) Prototype sdkenv CLI alpha v0.1 with bootstrap + proxy + mode toggle (owner: Marcus, 2-week spike).
2) Add curated fixture set for simple-chat and embedder-demo (owner: Sofia, 1 week).
3) Ship onboarding checklist and instrument time-to-first-stream telemetry (owner: Aisha, 2 weeks).
4) Run a 2-week trial with 5 new hires and collect qualitative feedback.

Appendix: micro-examples (copyable)
Node quick run (example):
const Redwood = require('@redwood/sdk')
const client = new Redwood({ endpoint: 'http://localhost:5400', token: process.env.SDKEVN_TOKEN })
(async () => {
  const stream = await client.chat.stream({ model: 'small-chat-test', messages:[{role:'user', content:'Summarize: product release notes'}] })
  for await (const chunk of stream) console.log(chunk.text)
})()

Curl streaming check (from terminal):
curl -i -N http://localhost:3000/api/chat -H "Authorization: Bearer $SDKEVN_TOKEN" -d '{"prompt":"hello"}'

If you take one thing away: invest in the first three minutes of a developer's life — that time compounds into faster iterations, fewer ci cycles, and happier contributors.
